title: What is a consumer group, and how does partition assignment work within and across groups?
shortTitle: Consumer groups and partition assignment within and across groups
keyPoints: A consumer group is a set of consumer instances sharing the same group id that cooperate to consume a topic's partitions.
Within a group, each partition is assigned to exactly one consumer, so each record is processed once by the group.
Across groups, every group independently receives all partitions and tracks its own offsets, enabling publish-subscribe semantics.
Partition assignment strategies include RangeAssignor, RoundRobinAssignor, StickyAssignor, and CooperativeStickyAssignor.
A group cannot have more active consumers than partitions; surplus consumers sit idle as hot standbys.
The group coordinator on a broker manages membership, heartbeats, and triggers rebalancing when consumers join or leave.

s1_definition.oneliner: Within a group, partitions are divided so each is owned by one consumer; across groups, every group gets all partitions independently.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Consumer group** – a set of consumer instances sharing the same `group.id` that cooperate to consume a topic's partitions, with each partition assigned to exactly one consumer in the group.
- **Group coordinator** – a broker role that manages consumer group membership, receives heartbeats, and triggers rebalances when the group changes.
- **Partition assignment strategy** – the algorithm that divides partitions among consumers in a group, including `RangeAssignor`, `RoundRobinAssignor`, `StickyAssignor`, and `CooperativeStickyAssignor`.
- **Rebalance** – the process of redistributing partition ownership when a consumer joins, leaves, or fails, temporarily pausing consumption.
- **`__consumer_offsets`** – the internal Kafka topic that stores committed offsets per consumer group per partition, enabling resume-from-where-you-left-off behavior.
s1_definition.analogy: Think of a consumer group as a team of clerks at National Bank of India who share one job, such as processing transactions. The team lead (group coordinator) hands each clerk a set of ledger drawers (partitions) so no two clerks on the same team touch the same drawer, and together they get through all the work once. A different team, say the fraud team, has its own lead and its own copy of all the drawers to read independently. Same records, two teams, each doing their own job without stepping on each other.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
Consumer Group: Within vs Across
=================================

Within a Group (settlement-group, 6 partitions):
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Group: settlement-group                        │
│                                                 │
│  Consumer A ──▶ P0, P1  (2 partitions)          │
│  Consumer B ──▶ P2, P3  (2 partitions)          │
│  Consumer C ──▶ P4, P5  (2 partitions)          │
│                                                 │
│  Each partition owned by exactly ONE consumer.   │
│  Each record processed ONCE by the group.        │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Across Groups (same topic, different groups):
┌─────────────────────┐  ┌─────────────────────┐
│ settlement-group    │  │ fraud-group          │
│ A->P0,P1  B->P2,P3 │  │ X->P0,P1  Y->P2,P3 │
│ C->P4,P5           │  │ Z->P4,P5            │
│ Own offsets: 500    │  │ Own offsets: 300     │
└─────────────────────┘  └─────────────────────┘
         │                         │
         │    Same topic data      │
         │    Independent offsets  │
         │    No interference      │
         ▼                         ▼
   Process once             Process once
   (settlement)             (fraud detection)
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
A consumer group is a set of consumer instances that share the same group id and cooperate to consume a topic. The key rule is that within a single group, each partition is assigned to exactly one consumer, so the group processes each record once while spreading the work across instances. At National Bank of India, the settlement-group has three instances that divide six partitions, each handling two, so the group processes transactions three times faster than a single consumer.

Across groups, assignment is completely independent. Each group has its own coordinator state and committed offsets, so the fraud-group and the audit-group both read every partition and track their own progress without interfering with the settlement-group. This is exactly how Kafka supports the publish-subscribe pattern: add a new group and it independently consumes the whole topic.

The assignment strategy and rebalancing mechanics are important for production stability. The CooperativeStickyAssignor minimizes disruption during rebalances by only moving the partitions that actually need to change owner. Monitoring consumer lag per group per partition tells you whether each team is keeping up with the event stream.

Remember one sentence: within a consumer group, each partition is owned by exactly one consumer for load-sharing, and across groups, every group independently reads all partitions for publish-subscribe.
